groups.passage: Solar panels can turn sunlight into electricity. Conventional solar panels are [[16]] crystallized silicon, the same material used in computer chips. But silicon is expensive and the panels are heavy. Facing this [[17]], engineers at a Japanese company have developed a thin-film flexible solar panel. The new panel is not the first of its [[18]], but it may be the most flexible—it bends like paper. At one kilogram per square meter, this new type of panel weighs one tenth of conventional solar panels. [[19]] means it could be used in novel places, such as the roof of a tent, the walls of a building, or the top of a bus. Sheets of the material could be used to make portable, rollable battery chargers for mobile electronic [[20]], like notebook computers or cellphones. As many countries are now pushing for green technology, the new flexible solar panels may spur a great demand.

tags.key_phrase: Facing this challenge（指前句 silicon is expensive and the panels are heavy）
That means ...（That 指前一句所述）

groups.passage:
During a money management class, a mother shared her young child’s idea about money. Her son believed that when she ran out of money all she had to do was go to a bank machine, put in her ATM card and money would come out. [[21]] the child didn’t quite understand was that his mother had to have money in the bank in the first place to get money out of the machine later.
It may surprise us how much our children already know about money. They learn by watching what their parents do with money. This starts at a very young age. Kids watch their parents [[22]] things at stores, write checks, use credit cards or even make donations. Children also learn that there are often strong [[23]] connected with money. They learn how their parents feel about money by the tone of voice they use and the look on their faces. [[24]], parents should ask themselves if they want their children to handle money the same way they do.
The long-term [[25]] of teaching children good money habits is well worth the effort. Those who learn good money management skills are more likely to become adults who make sound financial decisions, avoid excessive debt, and reach their financial goals.

tags.key_phrase: What the child didn’t quite understand was that ...（What 名詞子句當主詞）

groups.passage: Over the years, the Great Barrier Reef, off Australia’s east coast, has grown to be 1,240 miles long. [[26]] up of 2,900 connected reefs, the area is home to thousands of plant and animal species. Much of the reef system is protected, [[27]] conservationists have long worried that not enough was being done to safeguard the area. On April 3, 2010, their concerns came true. A cargo ship, Shen Neng 1, left Australia for China, carrying 65,000 tons of coal. Five hours into its [[28]], the vessel strayed from its shipping lane. It plowed through a protected reef, destroying everything in its path. The damage covered an area as large as five football fields. With more and more ships [[29]] the Great Barrier Reef, experts fear an even bigger accident is bound to happen. Fortunately, tougher rules are expected to [[30]] effect in July 2011. There are high hopes that these rules will prevent similar accidents from happening.

sections.title: 三、文意選填（占10分）
sections.instructions: 說明：第31題至第40題，每題一個空格，請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (J) 選項中分別選出最適當者，並將其英文字母代號畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對得1分；未作答、答錯、或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

groups.passage:
Many teenagers have trouble getting up early in the morning. Some people believe that they are [[31]] to get up early all because of laziness. But it is not necessarily the case. Sleep experts say this teen behavior actually has a physical [[32]]: Teenagers are biologically programmed to go to sleep later and get up later than other age groups.
Teenagers normally don’t feel sleepy until 11 p.m. or later. And they cannot [[33]] until 8:00 a.m. because they need about nine hours of sleep a night. Obviously, their biological rhythm is [[34]] an early school start time. With most high schools starting before 7:30 a.m., teenagers have to get up as early as 6:30 a.m. or so. They are, [[35]], not getting the sleep they need.
In fact, surveys show that half the teenagers in the USA are missing one to 1½ hours of sleep every school night. The [[36]] of sleep has negative effects on almost all aspects of teens’ lives. Their academic, athletic, and even driving performances may drop [[37]] insufficient sleep. They also more easily get annoyed and depressed. To meet teens’ sleep needs, many school districts in the USA changed the school start time, [[38]] children to start later in the morning. This change has brought many positive results, [[39]], a decrease in visits to health centers and rest requests. Besides, students reported that they felt less sleepy and were more [[40]] during the day. Teachers also found that there was a more positive mood in the classroom.

tags.topic: teenagers’ sleep needs and later school start times

sections.title: 四、閱讀測驗（占32分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第41題至第56題，每題4個選項，請分別根據各篇文章之文意選出最適當的一個答案，畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對得2分；未作答、答錯、或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

groups.passage:
The ocarina, a flute-like musical instrument, has been around since the Stone Age. Ocarinas have been found in Africa, Asia, Europe, and South America. Most of those found were made from clay while some were made of bone, wood, and other materials. Because they produce sounds similar to bird calls, ocarinas have been credited with magical powers.
One variation of the ocarina in Chinese culture is the xun, which has a history of more than 7,000 years. It is made of earthenware clay and often comes in the shape of an egg. At various times in Chinese music history, the instrument has played an important role in the imperial orchestra for religious worship and palace entertainment.
Ocarinas were also found to serve various purposes in other cultures. For example, the Mayans of South America, like the Chinese, also used ocarinas for special ceremonies. From there European travelers brought this South American “whistle” back, and it was later modified to play the Western scale. In the 1800s, Italy saw the greatest development of the ocarina, where musicians formed groups to play ocarinas of various sizes. During World War II the ocarina was introduced to the United States and playing it became a pastime for soldiers.
In the 20th century, the ocarina was popular among the general public, and the application of ocarina music was extended to video games. In 1999, Nintendo released Zelda: the Ocarina of Time, the most popular video game of all time. The game features a character named Link who plays songs on an ocarina in order to go to different areas of the game.

groups.passage: A recent study examined the emotional bond between parents and their children. The researchers surveyed 1,256 students in Canada, France, and Italy. Professor Michel Claes, the leader of the research team, explained why they selected the three countries: “We chose French-Canadians because they share the same language as the French, and originally came from France. They share certain values. Italy was included because it was considered to have similar, strong, important family values.” The most important finding of the study was the difference between Canadians and the others. Canadian parents value independence and are more willing to enter discussions with their children when there are disagreements. They are more tolerant and exercise less control. In contrast, Italian parents are stricter and more demanding. French parents are somewhere in the middle. In other words, Canadian parents are more lenient with their children than parents in France and Italy. Professor Claes explained the finding in terms of differences in education. “North America has its own democratic and educational values, which promote individualization. Tolerance and comprehension are encouraged and we exclude systems of control. Italy, on the other hand, promotes the respect of authority, control, and the need for permission,” he said. Children from all three countries described their mothers as warm and open. Italian and Canadian children had similar feelings about their fathers and reported high levels of emotional bonding. But French fathers were seen by their children as being more distant. It seemed that the relationships of French mothers with their children were becoming closer over time; but fathers maintained a certain distance and coldness.

groups.passage: Not long ago, joy wasn’t considered serious enough for psychologists to study. These scientists traditionally helped people with depression or other mental illnesses. But today, happiness is a hot subject of research. As part of a growing field called positive psychology, more and more researchers are looking for ways to help people become happier. However, the field of positive psychology has to overcome significant obstacles. For one thing, it’s difficult to scientifically gauge happiness. It’s also hard to compare one person’s sense of well-being with another’s. For example, if your best friend says she feels great, but she’s crying a lot and acting more depressed than usual, would you rate her as happy or sad for the purposes of a scientific study? Likewise, on a scale of 1 to 10, how can we be sure that my “8” is happier than your “6” ? In recent years, however, researchers have developed a few accurate measurements of happiness. One of the techniques involves looking at how often people genuinely smile in their daily lives. It’s easy to tell real smiles from the fake smiles people put on for photographs. Genuine smiles engage the corners of the eyes and involve muscles around the mouth that fake smilers can’t control. With the help of these techniques, recent studies have found that the happiest people are those who frequently do kind things for both friends and strangers. Other research-backed happiness boosters include keeping a diary of your future dreams, setting and pursuing goals, making friends and family members a big part of your life, expressing optimism about your future, extending gratitude to people who help you, and exercising regularly.

groups.passage:
Video games have been blamed for many of the ills of the world. Parents complain that violent games make their children antisocial, violent, shallow, and overweight. Educators worry that video games are breeding a generation that cannot sustain their concentration.
However, a recent study from cognitive science suggests that there may be a benefit in playing some action games. The research, published in Current Biology, reports that video gamers make faster and more accurate decisions. What was particularly interesting was that the faster reaction times could also be acquired by non-video gamers with 50 hours of training over a few weeks. But for the benefits to increase, they had to play a particular sort of game. Only those who played fast-moving action video games such as “Call of Duty 2” and “Unreal Tournament” saw an improvement in their decision-making skills. Rather ironically, players of “The Sims 2,” a game where one has to decide how to organize an entire simulated world, did not show the same benefit.
The precise reason for this effect is still unknown. What is known, however, is that people make decisions based on probabilities, which are constantly being calculated and refined in their heads. The brain collects small pieces of information, eventually gathering enough to make an accurate decision. When driving a car, for example, these many probabilities will be compared to make decisions such as whether or not to brake. The more efficient a person is at collecting visual and auditory information, the faster he or she will become ready to make a decision.

options.D: To report new findings on the effect of playing video games.

options.D: Playing some video games may help us improve our decision-making skills.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the last paragraph?

options.C: The influence of video games on decision making has been positively proved.
options.D: Decision making is based on information gathered and compared in the brain.

sections.title: 二、英文作文（占20分）
sections.instructions:
說明︰1.依提示在「答案卷」上寫一篇英文作文。
2.文長至少120個單詞（words）。

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem:
提示︰新聞報導鄰國大地震，災情嚴重，請寫一封信給在當地的朋友（英文名字必須假設為 Tom 或 Kelly），表達慰問之意。第一段敘述自己從新聞報導上得知該地震的災情訊息；第二段表達自己對天災的感受（或分享經驗）並表達慰問之意。
請注意：為避免評分困擾，信末必須使用 John 或 Susan 署名，不得使用自己真實的中文或英文名字。
questions.scoring_notes:
英文作文評分指標（考試說明 other-5.pdf 印刷頁碼第13頁〔PDF 第17頁〕；考試說明所列之一般評分指標，非本參考試卷專屬的評分原則。表格依「項目：等級（分數）＝描述」轉成文字）
內容：優（5-4分）＝主題(句)清楚切題，並有具體、完整的相關細節支持。／可（3分）＝主題不夠清楚或突顯，部分相關敘述發展不全。／差（2-1分）＝主題不明，大部分相關敘述發展不全或與主題無關。／劣（0分）＝文不對題或沒寫(凡文不對題或沒寫者，其他各項均以零分計算)。
組織：優（5-4分）＝重點分明，有開頭、發展、結尾，前後連貫，轉承語使用得當。／可（3分）＝重點安排不妥，前後發展比例與轉承語使用欠妥。／差（2-1分）＝重點不明、前後不連貫。／劣（0分）＝全文毫無組織或未按提示寫作。
文法、句構：優（4分）＝全文幾無文法錯誤，文句結構富變化。／可（3分）＝文法錯誤少，且未影響文意之表達。／差（2-1分）＝文法錯誤多，且明顯影響文意之表達。／劣（0分）＝全文文法錯誤嚴重，導致文意不明。
字彙、拼字：優（4分）＝用字精確、得宜，且幾無拼字錯誤。／可（3分）＝字詞單調、重複，用字偶有不當，少許拼字錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。／差（2-1分）＝用字、拼字錯誤多，明顯影響文意之表達。／劣（0分）＝只寫出或抄襲與題意有關的零碎字詞。
體例：優、可（2分，原表兩欄合併）＝格式、標點、大小寫幾無錯誤。／差（1分）＝格式、標點、大小寫等有錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。／劣（0分）＝違背基本的寫作體例或格式，標點、大小寫等錯誤甚多。
（考試說明 other-5.pdf「試題舉例 1.簡函寫作」收錄同一主題的100年度研究用試卷版本〔提示為「Susan 從新聞報導得知日本大地震，災情嚴重，想寫一封信給在日本的朋友 Tom，表達慰問之意。請依照下列所附書信格式書寫這封信。」，並附日期 April 20, 2011、稱呼 Dear Tom,、結尾 Love, Susan 的書信格式〕，說明：本題主要評量考生能否運用詞彙、語法、修辭知識，寫出切合主題，達成特定目的之簡函。此思考過程至少符合「2-4：能評估不同資訊，提出合理的判斷或建議」與「2-5：能整合、規劃相關資訊及資源，並發揮創意」的邏輯思考與判斷能力。）

extraction.method: pdftotext -layout 與 pdftotext（raw）擷取 paper-2.pdf，以程式依題組切分選文、題幹、選項（空格以題號序列定位後轉成 [[題號]]，文字層的 CJK 相容字元以 NFC 還原），再以程式把每段英文與 raw／layout 兩種文字層逐詞比對；Read 逐頁看 paper-2.pdf 全部8頁頁面影像，確認段落、空格位置、粗體／斜體與說明框文字；選擇題答案取自 answer-2.pdf（pdftotext＋頁面影像逐題核對），中譯英參考答案依 answer-2.pdf 第2頁頁面影像確認大括號層次後展開；考試說明 other-5.pdf（pdftotext＋PDF 第15–18頁〔印刷頁碼11–14〕頁面影像，作文評分指標表以 pdftoppm 220dpi 放大）只用來核對答案、補充 scoring_notes 與標註；另以 8-gram 比對 data/raw/ceec 下學測83–115、指考91–110全部題本 paper-1.pdf，找出沿用的歷屆試題；建檔腳本放 scratchpad，未進 repo；查證者（verifier）另以 pdftotext -layout／raw 重新擷取，以程式將每題「題號＋題幹＋選項」整串、選項庫整串與每篇選文全文對文字層做逐字子字串比對並核對字數、段落數、[[題號]] 位置與底線長度，Read 看題本全部頁面、答案檔全部頁面與考試說明相關頁面影像逐題核對答案、中譯英大括號展開與作文評分指標表
issues: 檔案拆分：units.json 的 ref-102 含兩份不同試卷——paper-1.pdf「指定科目考試參考試卷（適用於99課綱）英文考科」（答案 answer-1.pdf）與 paper-2.pdf「學科能力測驗參考試卷（適用於99課綱）英文考科」（答案 answer-2.pdf）。依同年多份試卷的規則分別輸出 ref-102-a（指考參考試卷）與 ref-102-b（學測參考試卷），exam 都填 reference，year 填 102（99課綱自102學年度施測）。

結構核對（gsat-spec.json legacy_gsat「94–110」期別，本卷為99課綱學測參考試卷）：與題本一致——詞彙題1–15（各1分）、綜合測驗16–30（3篇×5題，各1分）、文意選填31–40（10個選項(A)–(J)，各1分）、閱讀測驗41–56（4篇×4題，各2分）、中譯英2題各4分、英文作文20分（至少120個單詞）；第壹部分72分＋第貳部分28分＝100分。大題名稱「詞彙題」「中譯英」與 spec「100起改稱中譯英」「102起改稱詞彙題」一致。第壹部分標題為「第壹部分：單選題（占72分）」，所以 sections 的 part 填「單選題」。封面「題型題數：第壹部分 單選題共 56 題；第貳部分 非選擇題共二大題」與內文一致；考試時間100分鐘（封面）。不倒扣（各大題說明：答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算）。
統計：參考試卷沒有正式施測，units.json 沒有 stats 檔，repo 中也找不到本卷的答對率或鑑別度，所以所有小題的 stats 都是 null，sources.stats 為空陣列；validator 的「整份考卷沒有任何統計資料」warning 由此而來，屬預期。沿用自歷屆試題的題目也沒有把原考試的統計複製過來（原考試的作答條件不同）。
答案來源：選擇題1–56取自 answer-2.pdf「英文考科參考答案」（看頁面影像逐題核對）。考試說明 other-5.pdf 以「100年度研究用試卷」為名收錄了本卷部分題目的早期版本，與本卷相同的題目答案都一致：詞彙第2題 B、文意選填31–40 FEHDAJCGIB、閱讀41–43 AAD（考試說明第44題的選項與本卷不同，不比較）。

考試說明的早期版本與本卷有文字差異，題目一律以題本為準：詞彙第2題選項(A) 原為 handle（本卷 produce）；第16–20題選文原為「To ___ this problem」（17題選項 show/defend/solve/detect）、「That means it could be used in novel places, ___ the roof of a tent…」（19題選項 such as/except for/due to/rather than）、「could also be used」「including notebook computers」；第31–40題選文原為「half of the teenagers」；第41–44題選文原為「magical power」「Italy saw the greatest development of the ocarina in the 1800s」「play on ocarinas」「Link that plays」，第42題題幹原為「How did the Chinese use ocarinas?」、第44題選項不同；中譯英第2題題目原為「學校應該提供一個好的環境，來幫助學生發展個人特質。」（多一個逗號），參考答案與本卷 answer-2 相同；作文的早期版本是 Susan 寫給日本朋友 Tom 並附書信格式，與本卷提示不同。

中譯英參考答案（answer-2.pdf 第2頁，大括號排版；看頁面影像確認括號層次）：scoring_notes 以 {A | B} 記號逐字保留原排版。第1題「We {should | must | have to} {know | be aware | realize | understand} that every {child | kid} is born with different interests and {talents. | gifts.}」：answer 取各括號第一個寫法，共 3×4×2×2＝48 種，accepted_answers 47 種（「be aware that」照官方保留）。第2題「Schools should provide {a good environment | good surroundings} to help students develop (their) {personal | individual} {characteristics. | traits.}」：answer 取各括號第一個寫法並保留可省略的 their（比照 ref-110／ref-115），共 2×2×2×2＝16 種，accepted_answers 15 種。v1.1：兩題各括號互不相依，改以 answer_segments 表示（第1題 7 段 48 種、第2題 6 段 16 種，(their) 以空字串表示可省略），展開結果與 answer＋accepted_answers 的集合相同；兩題 answer_is_composite: true。

評分原則：本卷沒有評分原則檔（units.json 沒有 scoring，sources.scoring 為空陣列）。中譯英 scoring_notes 收錄 answer-2.pdf 的參考答案排版，以及考試說明 other-5.pdf 對同一題的試題說明（註明出處）。英文作文 scoring_notes 收錄考試說明 other-5.pdf 的「英文作文評分指標」表（內容、組織各5分，文法句構、字彙拼字各4分，體例2分；看頁面影像確認，表格依「項目：等級（分數）＝描述」轉成文字，「體例」列優、可兩欄在原表合併）與簡函寫作試題舉例的說明；考試說明的作文提示是早期版本，已在 scoring_notes 註明。官方沒有範文，作文 answer 為 null。

沿用的歷屆試題：以 8-gram 比對 data/raw/ceec 下學測83–115、指考91–110全部題本，只找到「According to the passage, which of the following statements is true about…」這類通用題幹，以及第26題的選項組合（To make／Make／Made／Making，gsat-84 第36題也用過，但選文不同），沒有找到被沿用的選文或題目。考試說明標示部分題目出自「100年度研究用試卷」，該試卷不在 repo 內。

原文排版照題本保留：第49–52題選文「your “6” ?」問號前有空格、第55題題幹「Current Biology , which」逗號前有空格（文字層與頁面影像都是如此）。詞彙題空格底線長度照文字層（第3、7、10、14題為6個底線，第8題為7個，其餘5個）。克漏字類空格前後因底線排版造成的空白已去除，例如「Facing this [[17]], engineers」「a physical [[32]]:」「They are, [[35]], not」。第31題空格在題本中緊接在 are 之後（「they are__31__」），寫成「they are [[31]] to get up」。題組前的「第 16 至 20 題為題組」等標示沒有放進 passage。

格式：選文與第47題的 we、選文與第49題的 gauge 為粗體，是題目所問的字，選文對應處以 … 標出並填 refers_to（題幹不另加標記）；第51與53題的 NOT（粗體）與斜體（選文與第42題選項的 xun、Zelda: the Ocarina of Time、選文與第55題的 Current Biology）沒有保留格式。作文「請注意」一句中「信末必須使用 John 或 Susan 署名」「不得使用自己真實的中文或英文名字」在題本加了底線強調，這不是題目在問的畫底線字，所以沒有用 標記。本卷沒有任何圖表。
作文提示的空白：PDF 文字層為「假設為 Tom」「或 Kelly」「使用 John 或 Susan 署名」，中英文之間有空白；「Tom」與「或」之間正好是換行，比照同句「John 或 Susan」補回一個空白，寫成「假設為 Tom 或 Kelly」。本卷沒有 Word 版可以核對。提示與「請注意」兩段以換行分開放在 stem。
題號：中譯英在題本印為 1.、2.，作文沒有題號；schema 要求 no 為整數，所以中譯英 no＝1、2，作文 no＝1，label 寫成「中譯英1」「中譯英2」「英文作文」，以免和詞彙題1、2重複（與 ref-110、ref-111、ref-115 相同做法）。validator 的「題號重複 [1, 2]」warning 由此而來，屬預期。

說明文字：冒號照文字層原樣——詞彙、綜合測驗、閱讀測驗、作文的說明與「提示︰」用「︰」(U+FE30)，文意選填、中譯英的說明與「請注意：」用「：」(U+FF1A)。文字層的 CJK 相容字元（如 U+F96F「說」、U+F98A「力」、U+F969「數」）已以 NFC 還原為一般漢字。大題標題在 PDF 中是字距加寬排版，title 去除了這些排版空白；文意選填說明「(A) 到 (J)」前後的空白照文字層保留。中譯英、作文說明的兩點以換行分開。第壹、第貳部分標題放在擴充欄位 parts（與 ast-103 相同做法）。

標註判斷：第17題 challenge 指前句「silicon is expensive and the panels are heavy」，標 discourse；第19題 That 指前一句整句，標 grammar／pronoun；第21題 What 引導名詞子句當主詞，標 noun_clause；第26題 Made up of 為過去分詞構句，標 participle；第37題 due to 依考試說明（因果關係）標 connective；第38題 allowing 依 allow + O + to V 的語意選答，標 word_meaning。閱讀：第46、50、56題問段落大意，標 main_idea；第47題問 we 指誰，官方答案為 (A) Canadian parents，標 reference；第48題標 detail；第52題標 inference；第54題標 purpose。sdgs：軟性太陽能板 [7, 9]、大堡礁貨輪事故 [14]、青少年睡眠 [3]、正向心理學與快樂 [3]、中譯英（尊重孩子天賦、學校環境）[4]、作文鄰國大地震 [11]（比照 gsat-94 地震題組）；其他為 []。
來源檔：other-5.pdf 與 other-7.pdf 是同一份「學科能力測驗英文考科考試說明（適用於99課綱）」（md5 相同），只列 other-5.pdf；other-6.pdf／other-8.pdf（學測英文考科命題方向，兩檔相同）已讀過，示例題目取自96學測，沒有收錄本卷試題，未使用。other-1–4 屬指考，用於 ref-102-a。

查證（verifier）：獨立重新核對，未發現需要修正的內容。(1) 第1–56題答案逐題對照 answer-2.pdf 第1頁（文字層＋頁面影像）全部一致；中譯英2題的 answer＋accepted_answers 以程式依 answer-2.pdf 第2頁大括號排版重新展開（48、16種組合）比對，集合完全相同。(2) 第1–30、41–56題「題號＋題幹＋(A)–(D)選項」整串與文意選填(A)–(J)選項庫整串，都與 pdftotext -layout 文字層逐字一致（只差排版空白），選項後接下一題號或大題標題，無截斷；詞彙題底線長度與文字層一致。(3) 8篇選文全文都是文字層「第 N 至 M 題為題組」與第一題之間的完整逐字子字串，字數 154/212/159/256/267/264/275/259 與 pdftotext 相同，段落數 1/3/1/3/4/3/4/3 與頁面影像縮排一致，[[16]]–[[40]] 位置正確；Read 看 paper-2.pdf 全部8頁影像確認（含 your “6” ?、Current Biology , 的空格）。(4) 大題標題、說明、部分標題、中譯英題目、作文提示與「請注意」與文字層一致；考試說明 other-5.pdf 第15–17頁影像核對中譯英試題說明、簡函寫作早期版本與作文評分指標表逐格內容，與 scoring_notes 一致。(5) 以 7-gram 比對 repo 內其他已解析考卷，只有通用題幹（Which of the following is NOT mentioned… 等）重疊，沒有沿用的選文或題目。本卷沒有統計檔，無法抽查統計。
